# RQ3 ablation results (Table VI, Section V-C and Fig. 3 of the paper)

**Sources in this package.** For Conduit and RWA: `docs/design/cpv-expansion/rq3-temporal-comparison.md` and `rq3-flat-comparison.md` (generated by `eval/ui_semantics/deepseek-ablation-20260913/ablation_compare.py`; machine-readable copies `eval/ui_semantics/deepseek-ablation-20260913/rq3-*-comparison.json`), `docs/design/cpv-expansion/rq1-audit-deepseek{,-temporal,-flat}/summary.md`, and `docs/design/cpv-expansion/rq3-evidence-dependence{,-temporal,-flat}-20260913.md` (generated by `evidence_dependence.py`). For Umami, Paperless-ngx and Ghost: `docs/design/subjects-expansion-20260919/rq3-{temporal,flat}-comparison.md` (generated by `eval/ui_semantics/subjects-ablation-20260921/ablation_compare_subjects.py`; machine-readable copies `eval/ui_semantics/subjects-ablation-20260921/rq3-*-comparison.json`) and `docs/design/subjects-expansion-20260919/rq1-audit-<subject>-{temporal,flat}/summary.md`. The README lists the commands that regenerate them.

**Configurations.** All three use the same inputs per subject, the same recordings, the same model settings (DeepSeek V4.1-Flash, reasoning effort high, three generation rounds merged by union, concurrency 48, probe budget 0), the same candidate oracle template set and the same M11–M14 validation pipeline; only the association information visible to candidate generation, and its organization, changes. *Full* is the complete approach. *Temporal* removes all explicit association structure from the view (data flows, dependency edges, rebinding evidence, API state differences, prerequisite hints, and the association references on the cards); the view is the central card plus a fixed temporal neighborhood of 16 requests before and after, keeping request groups, page-state differences, negative facts and prerequisite scopes. *Flat* further removes UI-action grouping, the neighborhood, page-state differences and negative facts, so the model sees individual requests in temporal order. Labels of the Conduit and RWA ablation suites: model-assisted initial review (prompt v2.1) plus author adjudication with the same rules A/B/C as their Full suite (`REVIEW-ADJUDICATIONS.md`); labels of the Umami, Paperless-ngx and Ghost ablation suites are the initial ones, and their Full rows carry the initial labels plus the three adjudicated items. RQ2 was not repeated on the ablation suites. Paperless-ngx compares a reduced suite of 32 inputs: `L1-DOCLIST-01/02/04` never completed M10 in the Full configuration and carry no test there, so they are excluded from all three configurations of that subject (`fixtures/recording_workflows/paperless_modular/inventory-ablation.json`).

**Run roots** (for each case the first root, in this order, whose union holds a complete M14 suite): Full = `deepseek-full-20260912/{conduit: m11fix-01; rwa: m11fix-02 > rerecord-01 > m11fix-01}`; Temporal = `deepseek-ablation-20260913/{conduit: temporal-01; rwa: temporal-retry-02 > temporal-01}`; Flat = `deepseek-ablation-20260913/{conduit: flat-01; rwa: flat-fix-01 > flat-retry-01 > flat-01}`. In the Temporal and Flat runs, RWA `L4-COMMENT-NOTIFY-01` was flagged as failed by a suite-level metadata-isolation heuristic although all of its stages M1–M14 completed; it is counted as completed, as in the main line.

For every retained business test whose candidate payload is available, `evidence_dependence.py` records which evidence the proposal cited (`evidence_refs`), whether the producer and observer requests belong to different UI actions or different users, and whether they lie more than 16 positions apart in recording order (only association-based expansion puts such a pair into one view). Denominators of the last three columns: relations with both a producer and an observer request.

## Paired comparison split by input, Conduit and RWA (does the difference come from the visible range?)

From `neighborhood_summary.outside_temporal_radius_related_request_count` of the cards in the Full run's evidence views, 14 of the 83 inputs have associated requests outside the ±16 neighborhood (Conduit `L3-COMMENT-01`, `L4-COMMENT-01`, `L4-FAVORITE-01`; RWA `L1-NOTIFY-01`, `L3-COMMENT-01`, `L3-REQUEST-ACCEPT-01`, `L3-REQUEST-REJECT-01`, `L4-COMMENT-NOTIFY-01`, `L4-LIKE-NOTIFY-01`, `L4-PAYMENT-NOTIFY-01`, `L4-REQUEST-NOTIFY-01`, `L4-REQUEST-REJECT-01`, `L4-THIRD-PARTY-COMMENT-01`, `L4-THIRD-PARTY-LIKE-01`); for the other 69 inputs the neighborhood already covers every associated request. Recomputed from the corrected audit files (C labels of `tests-labeled.jsonl`, `has_correct_target` of `targets.jsonl`):

| Configuration | Subset | Inputs | Correct business instances, Full → configuration | Primary target checked, Full → configuration | Paired: improved / degraded / same |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|
| Temporal | neighborhood covers all associated requests | 69 | 516 → 357 | 34 → 19 | 13 / 35 / 21 |
| Temporal | associated requests outside the neighborhood | 14 | 526 → 286 | 14 → 14 | 0 / 14 / 0 |
| Flat | neighborhood covers all associated requests | 69 | 516 → 229 | 34 → 0 | 4 / 42 / 23 |
| Flat | associated requests outside the neighborhood | 14 | 526 → 130 | 14 → 2 | 0 / 13 / 1 |

Section V-C of the paper cites the two Temporal rows: the decrease is as clear on the 69 inputs whose associated requests were all visible, so the difference between Temporal and Full does not mainly come from the visible range.

## Reading of the results (interpretation)

1. On Conduit and RWA both steps decrease monotonically: correct business relations Conduit 322 → 238 → 203 and RWA 720 → 405 → 156; correct semantic groups 182 → 95 → 87 and 433 → 274 → 139; cases with the primary target checked 48/71 → 33/71 → 2/71. In the per-input pairing, degradations dominate (Conduit 23/31 and 24/31, RWA 26/40 and 31/40); improvements occur on few inputs and are small.
2. On Umami, Paperless-ngx and Ghost, Temporal loses 18% (110 → 90), 26% (444 → 327) and 38% (596 → 371) of the correct business instances, and degradations dominate the pairing on Paperless-ngx and Ghost. Flat, however, retains *more* correct business instances than Full on all three (218, 507, 833). The surplus is single-response checks and read–read query relations: Umami V2 44 → 173, Paperless-ngx V2 290 → 446, Ghost V3 563 → 732. The relations that connect a write to its effects fall in every configuration step and on every subject (the table above): 894 → 520 → 265 over the five subjects. This is the quantity Section V-C reports, because it is the one the ablation is about.
3. With less organization the model proposes more candidates, not fewer (Conduit 698 → 979 → 1,471; RWA 1,982 → 3,328 → 4,611; Umami 265 → 273 → 1,411; Paperless-ngx 956 → 842 → 2,156; Ghost 1,025 → 908 → 2,082), and most of the surplus lands in the structural-constraint layer (Conduit 225 → 536 → 997; RWA 888 → 2,216 → 3,392; Umami 23 → 27 → 289; Paperless-ngx 294 → 272 → 1,212; Ghost 150 → 186 → 472): without associations and neighborhoods the model tends towards "field present / of type" assertions that need no cross-request evidence. Temporal is the exception on the three subjects whose Temporal run admitted fewer candidates than Full.
4. The error rate stays low as organization is removed on Conduit and RWA (E after adjudication 5/1,047 → 1/644 → 0/359): execution validation (M11–M14) keeps incorrect relations out of the retained set. On the other three subjects, whose labels are the initial ones, the counts are 0/110 → 2/92 → 0/219 (Umami), 0/444 → 1/328 → 1/508 (Paperless-ngx) and 2/598 → 1/372 → 10/843 (Ghost); the ten Flat instances of Ghost are the largest single group and the only place where the rate rises noticeably.
5. Cost: on Conduit and RWA, Temporal saves about a third of the prompt tokens compared with Full (91.4M → 60.8M), whereas Flat rises again (89.1M): one card per request and no neighborhood means more screening and detail batches, so "less organization" is not "cheaper". The same shape appears on the other three subjects (Umami 11.0 → 9.2 → 30.1M, Paperless-ngx 29.3 → 12.4 → 63.7M, Ghost 36.2 → 21.3 → 51.7M prompt tokens).
6. Limitations: a single model (DeepSeek V4.1-Flash), a single run per configuration (the three-round union has sampling variance), model-assisted labels (adjudicated for Conduit and RWA, initial for the other three subjects); the ±16 window of Temporal is the method's existing constant, not a tuned value.

## Process notes

Conduit and RWA:

- Temporal: generated 06:38–08:54 (2026-09-13). RWA `L2-ONBOARD-02` failed in the first round on a malformed model reply (a literal `v1` for the input-version field); a retry at 12:16 exhausted its budget on network errors during summary screening; the second retry completed at 20:11–20:22 (23 retained tests, all structural constraints).
- Flat: generated 08:54–12:09. Three RWA cases failed (two on model replies that violated the frozen answer structure, one on a KeyError in the M13 relation closure); after the corresponding pipeline fixes, two cases were rerun at 20:22–21:03 and one was continued from its frozen candidates at 21:04; all completed.
- Evaluation: a first evaluation that had exported both suites into one directory was discarded and redone per configuration (19:34–19:58); after the retries both configurations were re-evaluated with the new roots taking precedence (21:04–21:07).
- Correction of 2026-09-15 (see `RUN-NOTES.md`): the tests of Temporal `L2-ONBOARD-02` (`rwa/temporal-retry-02`, 23 tests) and Flat `L1-BANK-03` (`rwa/flat-fix-01`, 44 tests) had no layer label in the first audit extraction (a stale export directory left by an earlier failed attempt, and a failed export of the continued run); they were re-exported, `rq1_extract` was rerun, the three newly appearing Flat business tests were reviewed with the same procedure (all C), and the summaries, primary-target judgements, paired comparison and evidence statistics were recomputed. The pre-correction audit files are kept under `snapshots/pre-layerfix-20260915/` in the two ablation audit directories. Changes: Temporal RWA structural constraints 2,193 → 2,216; Flat RWA business 153 → 156, structural 3,351 → 3,392, correct 153 → 156, correct semantic groups 136 → 139, cases with ≥ 1 correct business assertion 29 → 30, strict C 140 → 143; total correct 356 → 359. Everything else unchanged.

Umami, Paperless-ngx and Ghost:

- The six runs were executed from a separate checkout of the pinned code (`<PAPER_CODE_WORKTREE>` in the shipped launchers) whose `src/` is commit `15cceb33f7` and whose Ghost fixtures are the ones the Ghost main-line run used, so the ablation compares against the Full runs on equal code. Its `eval/` directories are the ones in this package.
- Three phases, one application instance per subject at a time, with a separate run lock per phase (`ACTIVE-ablation-{temporal,phase2,phase3}.json`, all validated against the real guard by `check_lock.py`): phase 1 Umami and Ghost Temporal (06:44–08:36), phase 2 Umami and Ghost Flat plus Paperless-ngx Temporal (08:36–12:06), phase 3 Paperless-ngx Flat (12:06–14:48). The per-phase status files (`run-{temporal,flat}.status`, `phase-driver.log`) and the suite run results (`run-<config>-<subject>.log`) are shipped.
- The first attempt at the Paperless-ngx Temporal run used the full recording root instead of the reduced one and was restarted against `recordings-ablation`; symlinked case directories were rejected by the recorded-case closure check, so the reduced recording root carries byte copies of the case directories.
- Ghost `L1-TAG-03` failed before M11 in the Temporal configuration. In the Full configuration that input has one structural test and no correct business assertion, so the paired comparison records it as *same*.
- No fault detection (RQ2) was run on these ablation suites, as for Conduit and RWA.
